content:
Apple is about to launch its flagship new phones, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. The Pro lineup's pricing will be a clear advantage, but the iPhone 18 Pro also outperforms the pricier Ultra model in several other areas.

#1: Main camera with variable aperture

Rumors suggest the iPhone 18 Pro's main camera will see a major upgrade, including the introduction of a variable aperture. However, the iPhone Ultra is not expected to feature this.

Rumors about a variable aperture have been circulating for a long time, but we still don't know exactly how Apple will implement it. This feature is expected to significantly improve Portrait mode performance and offer deeper depth-of-field control. Night photography performance may also see notable gains.

The components required for a variable aperture are expected to be larger than the current main camera. Therefore, the ultra-thin iPhone Ultra is believed to be out of luck when it comes to this feature.

#2: Pro Max battery life reaches new highs

According to regulatory filings, the iPhone Ultra's battery life should be decent. But the Pro lineup—namely the iPhone 18 Pro Max—will still offer the longest battery life of any iPhone to date.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max's physical battery is reportedly 10% larger than that of the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and will benefit from efficiency gains brought by the A20 Pro and C2 chips. As a result, its battery life will easily be the best of any iPhone.

Due to its unique foldable design, it's hard to judge the iPhone Ultra's battery life based on specs alone. But the ultra-slim body and smaller physical battery undoubtedly make it impossible to keep up with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

#3: Face ID

This is the first time in years that a new flagship iPhone model will not feature Face ID. The iPhone Ultra will only support Touch ID.

Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro will continue to use the Face ID system that has been around for nearly a decade.

Apple is reportedly unable to make enough room for Face ID components inside the ultra-thin iPhone Ultra body. Proper support would require two sets of components—one for the outer display and another for the inner display. So when it comes to authentication, the iPhone 18 Pro will have a clear advantage.

#4: Telephoto lens

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue to be the only models with a telephoto lens. The iPhone Ultra will feature main and ultrawide cameras, but no telephoto lens with optical zoom support.

For many users who rely on telephoto capabilities, this could be a significant difference. Especially since Apple is reportedly further enhancing the telephoto lens this year with a wider aperture.

If you're after the most advanced camera system, the iPhone 18 Pro is clearly the way to go.

Bonus: The traditional iPhone experience

This isn't a technical feature, but it's worth mentioning. For many users, the "traditional" iPhone experience offered by the iPhone 18 Pro is a major advantage in itself.

The iPhone Ultra will be unlike any model before it. The size and shape of the inner and outer displays will feel foreign for an iPhone. Instead of using a single display like before, users will need to constantly fold and unfold the device, or take some time to adapt.

The current iPhone form factor is a beloved product. While foldable phones certainly have their fans, I'd wager that for the average consumer (who may have never heard of 9to5Mac), it's the traditional iPhone design of the iPhone 18 Pro that appeals to them.

Which new iPhone model are you planning to buy this fall? Let us know in the comments.
